title: Build depth with scale and spacing, not glow
intent: Get separation from size, weight, and space so the page holds up on any background and in both colour modes.
when_to_use: an expressive page needs layers or focus without a saturated halo
the page must survive a light mode and a dark mode
when_not_to_use: the design has a real light source model, as in a rendered scene or a photographed object, where a directed highlight belongs to the subject
the surface is a dense tool where elevation signals interaction and a flat treatment would hide the affordance
rules: no box shadow or filter blur uses a saturated colour; shadows stay neutral and low alpha
no gradient between two hues exists anywhere in the artifact
a gradient, if used at all, runs between two steps of one neutral ramp and covers at most one full bleed band, never a button or a card
separation is carried by at least one of: a size step, a weight step, a spacing step, or a single neutral border
trade_off: Flat neutral depth is quiet: the page loses the instant richness a glow gives on a dark hero, and every layer must be earned by composition.
failure_mode: Neutral shadows are applied everywhere at the same alpha, so the whole page floats and no element reads as nearer than any other.

example.brief: Dark product page that needs cards to read as layers.
example.ruling: Cards separate by a one step lighter neutral surface, a wider spacing step, and a 1px neutral border. No coloured blur, no two hue gradient, and both colour modes resolve from the same token set.
